reason: The quota row 'Access token | 5 minutes – 1 day' under 'Amazon Cognito user pools session validity parameters' gives exactly the settable range 5 minutes to 1 day for user pool access tokens.
The quota row 'Authentication session token | 3 minutes – 15 minutes' under the user pools session validity parameters heading states the 3 to 15 minute range.

The case study quotes state hCIAM validates registration and login, runs on Amazon Cognito, uses AWS WAF Bot Control against bot traffic, 2 million requests with around 13,000 rejected on a regular day, and 2.1 million processed with 250,000 false requests rejected on the second bot event.

The document history row dated September 12, 2024 says MFA codes can be sent by email message with advanced security features, and the feature plans table lists 'MFA with email one-time codes' as Essentials + Plus.
The document history row dated July 2, 2026 says verbatim that you can now manage provisioned limits for your user pool with the Amazon Cognito provisioning APIs.
The Cognito document history row dated February 1, 2024, linked to the user pools SAML IdP page, says you can now sign SAML requests, encrypt SAML responses, and set up IdP-initiated SAML SSO.

The FAQ says the user pools SKU and Essentials SKU are free for the first 10,000 MAUs, the pricing page scopes it to users signing in directly or through a social IdP per month per account or organization, and the pricing note gives the 50,000 MAU free tier for user pools created on or before 10:00am PT, November 22, 2024.

The quotes state the two flows (enhanced and basic), that enhanced manages role selection (default role, ABAC or RBAC) and credentials retrieval with credentials valid for one hour, and that in the basic flow your application selects the IAM role.

The identity pools request rate table gives GetCredentialsForIdentity (enhanced workflow) a default of 200 RPS, adjustable via the account team, and footnote 1 says the default is the minimum across Regions in the account and may be higher in some Regions.
The identity pools request rate table gives GetId a default of 25 RPS, adjustable via the account team, and footnote 1 supports the minimum-across-Regions qualifier.

The quotes say a trust policy should make each role assumable only by Cognito for authenticated users of the pool, and describe the example policy: federated users from cognito-identity.amazonaws.com, aud restricted to the identity pool ID, and an amr array member with value authenticated.

The quotes say rules are evaluated in order and the first matching rule's role is used unless CustomRoleArn overrides, and when no rule matches the Role resolution setting applies either Use default authenticated role or Deny request.

The quota row gives the hosted UI session cookie 1 hour, and the managed login page says a cookie set after sign-in with the login pages or a third-party provider allows sign-in with the same method for one hour and that authenticating with the cookie doesn't reset its duration.
The Essentials pricing example line says verbatim 'Price / MAU charged above the free tier for Essentials tier = $0.015', and the claim is framed as the AWS pricing example.
The Plus pricing example quotes bill all 950,000 MAUs above a 0 MAU free tier and compute the bill as $0.020 x 950,000, so every MAU is billed at $0.020 in that example.
The pricing quote scopes the 10,000 MAU free tier to users signing in directly or via a social IdP, applicable to Lite or Essentials, and says there is no free tier for the Plus tier.

The PrivateLink page says all user pools API operations work through the interface endpoint but not OAuth 2.0 authorization server operations, lists client credentials M2M from the token endpoint and managed login/classic hosted UI sign-in as not supported, and says GetClientToken M2M is supported because it needs no user pool domain.
The RBAC page says up to 25 rules per user pool or other authentication provider configured for an identity pool and that the limit is not adjustable; the quota table row (25, Adjustable No) agrees.
The refresh token page says REFRESH_TOKEN_AUTH isn't available in app clients with refresh token rotation enabled and that app clients with rotation active use GetTokensFromRefreshToken.

The FAQ quote describes the Sync store as a key/value pair store linked to a Cognito identity with no limit to identities in identity pools and sync store, and the availability page says Cognito Sync is no longer open to new customers; the claim attributes the description to the FAQ.

The What's New post dated Oct 2, 2025 says customers can upgrade Managed Microsoft AD from Standard to Enterprise Edition through the UpdateDirectorySetup API and that the self-service upgrade eliminates support tickets.

The What's New post dated Apr 1, 2026 says Multi-Region replication is available in opt-in Regions where Managed Microsoft AD is available except Middle East (UAE) and Middle East (Bahrain), paid hourly per domain controller per Region plus cross-Region data transfer; the availability condition is kept in the qualifiers.

The quotes say the default inbound rules allow only AD ports from the VPC's primary IPv4 or IPv6 CIDR, the ENIs have no Elastic IPs and you have no permission to attach one, so by default only the local VPC can communicate; the context confirms the rules can be changed.

The quota table gives default shared domains of 25 (Standard), 500 (Enterprise) and 125 (Hybrid), the footnote defines it as accounts a directory can be shared to, and the August 2025 What's New post gives the earlier 5 and 125 limits.

The 'Which to choose' row recommends Managed Microsoft AD Standard/Enterprise for actual Microsoft AD or LDAP for Linux apps, Hybrid Edition to extend self-managed AD, AD Connector when you only need on-premises users to log in (and to join EC2 instances), Simple AD for low-scale low-cost basic AD compatibility; the Simple AD notice supports the closing sentence.
The 'I develop SaaS applications' row says verbatim to use Amazon Cognito for high-scale SaaS applications needing a scalable directory for subscribers that works with social media identities.

The availability constraints list, with an organization instance present, requires administrator permission (after November 15, 2023) or manual enablement (before November 15, 2023), and then all of: no preventing SCP, no existing instance in the account in any Region, and a Region where IAM Identity Center is available.

The organization instance benefits list says it supports all features including multi-account permissions, customer managed applications and multi-Region replication, and gives central control of account instance creation as long as the instance isn't in an opt-in Region (disabled by default).

The FAQ quotes define permission sets as a collection of permissions modelled on AWS managed policies for job functions or any AWS managed policies, say they can be fully customized, and say IAM Identity Center applies them to the selected accounts automatically.

The revoke procedure quotes assume a deny-all policy in an SCP, add the user ID to the Deny policy, leave it for at least 12 hours or the active role session regains its actions, and say after 12 hours active sessions expire.

The customer managed applications quotes say you can assign access to SAML 2.0 applications, connected to an organization instance, including Connect Customer and AWS Client VPN which integrate exclusively using SAML, and that JWT-capable apps can use trusted identity propagation to request access to data in AWS services on behalf of users.

The quote states verbatim that with trusted identity propagation Amazon Quick can share a user's identity with Amazon Redshift and authorize access based on it, and CloudTrail events are logged based on the user and the actions the user initiated.

The user interactive sessions page says the default duration is 8 hours and a different duration from 15 minutes to 90 days can be set; the context ties these sessions to the AWS access portal sign-in.
